questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking country and rich culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Except accommodation

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The office responsible for incoming mail at Trinity was very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Very difficult

I would recommend starting your search early and trying to find accommodation through the college, as they can put you in contact with locals who rent out rooms. This is usually much cheaper than student accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The buses are nice, but they take quite a long time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was super difficult to find and it was very expensive

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They were very helpful.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to get an offer signed which you get by sending some info. then you have to sign up for classes online. Which is done through a portal, which opens up at a certain time. I cant remember when, but I remember feeling well informed.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The mail incoming erasmus students was very helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Make sure the classes are in the right semester. 

And take classes that are worth 10 ects points (most are worth 5) the level didn't feel too high nor the workload, and i was very happy with the subjects

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They felt advanced, but not more than any subject you could encounter at upch

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less classes and more self-studying

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
SOU4401 CONFLICT STUDIES
SOU4405 LABOUR MARKETS, GENDER & INSTITUTIONS 1
SOU44071 Advanced Methods of Sociological Data Science

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Conflict Studies. It focused on environmental sociology and was very in-depth. It also made me realise how little attention environmental sociology receives at UPCH, which is quite ridiculous considering how important the topic is for society and how many social problems it encompasses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many societies, but a little lackluster in the sports department

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: a lot of societies (theater, food, language ect.)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going outside the city - it was super beautiful and i regret i didn't do it more

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: belfast, cork, widlow mountains

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The Irish are quite curious and friendly, but also a little reserved at first. Once you get to know them, though, they’re very warm and easy to talk to

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People were very polite and used a lot of expressions like “thanks, love” and things like that. Apart from that, I didn’t really notice anything big

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Chatty and pub culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Find accommodation early, take 10 ects point subjects and make friends with the other erasmus students from ur classes. 

I did want to make more local friends, but realisticlly the other exchange students will likely be ur friends since they are also looking for friends and the also have a lot of time to do stuff

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The busses are very cheap for students and people under 25. But you have to order online. You refill the "leap cards" and the spars.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made and the classes, were i had a lot of time to study in depth

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Accommodation

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
